overall: The AG found the Halifax Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by approving 2021 meeting minutes nearly a year late without good cause, but found no violation in the revised-notice posting-time allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the revised notice for the Nov. 9, 2022 meeting omitted the date and time the original notice was posted.
allegations.key_passage: A public body is only required to indicate the original and revised posting times on a revised notice if it is revised within 48 hours of the noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve minutes of its Nov. 23, 2021 and Nov. 30, 2021 meetings, approving them nearly a year later.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board failed to timely approve the meeting minutes for November 23, 2021, and November 30, 2021.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future determination may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
